natural: Standing by the pool envying the fish

meaning.en: To wish for something without taking action to get it.
meaning.zh: 站在水边想得到鱼。比喻只有愿望而不去实干，就无济于事。

examples.zh: 临渊羡鱼，不如退而结网。
examples.en: Rather than envy the fish from the bank, go home and weave a net.

examples.zh: 光羡慕别人成功是临渊羡鱼，要自己努力。
examples.en: Just envying others' success gets you nowhere — work for it yourself.

story.en: Dong Zhongshu quoted the saying: "Better to go home and weave a net than to stand by the pool envying the fish."
story.zh: 《汉书·董仲舒传》："古人有言曰：'临渊羡鱼，不如退而结网。'"

usage.en: Usually with 不如退而结网.
usage.zh: 常与"不如退而结网"连用。

natural: Cutting iron like mud

meaning.en: (Of a blade) razor-sharp.
meaning.zh: 切削铁器像削泥土一样。形容刀剑极其锋利。

examples.zh: 这把宝剑削铁如泥。
examples.en: This sword cuts through iron like butter.

examples.zh: 传说干将莫邪剑削铁如泥。
examples.en: Legend says the Ganjiang and Moye swords were razor-sharp.

natural: Covering one's head and fleeing like a rat

meaning.en: To flee in panic.
meaning.zh: 抱着头像老鼠那样逃窜。形容狼狈逃跑。

equivalents: flee with one's tail between one's legs

examples.zh: 警察一来，小偷们抱头鼠窜。
examples.en: When the police arrived, the thieves scurried away.

examples.zh: 敌军被打得抱头鼠窜。
examples.en: The enemy fled in panic.

natural: Old in treachery and great in cunning

meaning.en: Wily and cunning; a crafty old fox.
meaning.zh: 形容人老于世故，非常奸诈狡猾。

examples.zh: 这个商人老奸巨猾，很难对付。
examples.en: The merchant is a wily old fox, hard to deal with.

examples.zh: 他老奸巨猾，从不留下证据。
examples.en: He's so crafty he never leaves evidence.

natural: Life is like a dream

meaning.en: Life is but a dream; life is fleeting.
meaning.zh: 人的一生像一场梦。形容人生短暂、变化无常。

examples.zh: 人生如梦，一尊还酹江月。
examples.en: Life is but a dream — let me pour a cup to the river moon.

examples.zh: 回首往事，他感叹人生如梦。
examples.en: Looking back, he sighed that life is but a dream.

origin.source: 宋·苏轼《念奴娇·赤壁怀古》

story.en: Su Shi's famous lyric at Red Cliff ends: "Life is like a dream; let me pour a cup of wine to the moon on the river" (人生如梦，一尊还酹江月).
story.zh: 苏轼《念奴娇·赤壁怀古》："人生如梦，一尊还酹江月。"

natural: Still smelling of milk

meaning.en: Wet behind the ears; young and inexperienced (contemptuous).
meaning.zh: 身上的奶腥气还没有完全退掉。对年轻人表示轻蔑的说法。

examples.zh: 你一个乳臭未干的毛孩子，懂什么？
examples.en: You're still wet behind the ears — what do you know?

examples.zh: 别看他乳臭未干，其实很有能力。
examples.en: He may look like a mere kid, but he's very capable.

story.en: Hearing who the enemy general was, Liu Bang scoffed: "His mouth still smells of milk" (是口尚乳臭) — he can't match my general Han Xin.
story.zh: 刘邦听说魏将是柏直，说："是口尚乳臭，不能当韩信。"

usage.en: Attributive or predicate. 臭 is xiù (smell). Contemptuous.
usage.zh: 多作定语、谓语。"臭"读 xiù。轻蔑语。

natural: Heart and mouth not the same

meaning.en: Saying one thing and thinking another.
meaning.zh: 心里想的和嘴上说的不一样。形容人的虚伪、诡诈。

equivalents: say one thing and mean another

examples.zh: 他心口不一，答应了也不会做。
examples.en: He's insincere — even if he agrees, he won't do it.

examples.zh: 心口不一的人难以让人信任。
examples.en: People who say one thing and mean another are hard to trust.

natural: So happy one forgets to go back

meaning.en: Having too much fun to want to leave.
meaning.zh: 非常快乐，竟忘记了回去。

equivalents: having too much fun to leave

examples.zh: 孩子们在游乐园里乐而忘返。
examples.en: The children were having too much fun at the amusement park to want to leave.

examples.zh: 这里风景优美，让人乐而忘返。
examples.en: The scenery here is so lovely you never want to leave.

natural: Shut the door and beat the dog

meaning.en: To trap the enemy and finish them off.
meaning.zh: 比喻把敌人围起来加以消灭。

examples.zh: 我们设下埋伏，关门打狗。
examples.en: We set an ambush to trap and finish them off.

examples.zh: 球队后撤防守，打算关门打狗。
examples.en: The team dropped back to box in the opposition.

usage.en: Predicate. Colloquial; one of the Thirty-Six Stratagems (关门捉贼).

natural: Bursting with self-importance

meaning.en: Full of oneself; cocky. Also: spirited and confident.
meaning.zh: 形容自以为优越而表现得十分得意的样子。也形容精神饱满。

examples.zh: 他穿上新制服，神气十足。
examples.en: In his new uniform he was strutting about.

examples.zh: 别看他现在神气十足，以前可落魄了。
examples.en: He may be cocky now, but he used to be down and out.

natural: Disaster arising within the palace walls

meaning.en: Trouble arising from within.
meaning.zh: 祸乱发生在家里。比喻内部发生祸乱。

examples.zh: 公司祸起萧墙，高管内斗。
examples.en: Trouble came from within as executives fought each other.

examples.zh: 历史上许多王朝都是祸起萧墙而亡。
examples.en: Many dynasties fell to enemies within.

story.en: When the Ji clan planned to attack the small state of Zhuanyu, Confucius said: "I fear the Ji family's trouble lies not in Zhuanyu, but within their own screen wall."
story.zh: 《论语·季氏》："吾恐季孙之忧，不在颛臾，而在萧墙之内也。"

usage.en: Predicate. 萧墙 = the screen wall inside a gate.
usage.zh: 多作谓语。"萧墙"指门内的屏风墙。

natural: Seeing what one has never seen

meaning.en: Never seen before; extraordinary.
meaning.zh: 看到了从来没有看到过的。形容事物非常稀罕。

examples.zh: 这次旅行让我见所未见，闻所未闻。
examples.en: This trip showed me things I'd never seen or heard of.

examples.zh: 这种奇观真是见所未见。
examples.en: I've never seen anything like this spectacle.

usage.en: Predicate. Often with 闻所未闻.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常与"闻所未闻"连用。

natural: Essential words without tedium

meaning.en: Concise and to the point.
meaning.zh: 说话或写文章简明扼要，不烦琐。

equivalents: brevity is the soul of wit

examples.zh: 他的发言要言不烦，切中要害。
examples.en: His speech was short and to the point.

examples.zh: 好的说明书应该要言不烦。
examples.en: Good instructions should be concise.

natural: A spark like a tiny star

meaning.en: A single spark (that can start a prairie fire); small beginnings with great potential.
meaning.zh: 一点儿小火星。比喻开始时显得弱小，但有旺盛生命力的新生事物。

equivalents: from little acorns mighty oaks grow

examples.zh: 星星之火，可以燎原。
examples.en: A single spark can start a prairie fire.

examples.zh: 这个小小的环保社团是星星之火，影响越来越大。
examples.en: The small green club was a single spark whose influence keeps growing.

origin.source: 《尚书·盘庚上》；毛泽东《星星之火，可以燎原》（1930）

story.en: The Book of Documents speaks of a fire "blazing across the plain" (若火之燎于原). Mao Zedong's 1930 letter titled "A Single Spark Can Start a Prairie Fire" made the full phrase famous.
story.zh: 《尚书·盘庚上》："若火之燎于原。"毛泽东1930年写《星星之火，可以燎原》一文，使此语广为流传。

usage.en: Usually with 可以燎原. 星星 here means tiny spark(s).

natural: Base and shameless

meaning.en: Despicable and shameless.
meaning.zh: 品质恶劣，不知羞耻。

examples.zh: 他用卑鄙无耻的手段陷害同事。
examples.en: He used despicable tactics to frame his colleague.

examples.zh: 这种卑鄙无耻的行为令人发指。
examples.en: Such shameless behaviour is outrageous.

natural: An old horse knows the way

meaning.en: The experienced know the way; experience is a good guide.
meaning.zh: 老马认识走过的道路。比喻有经验的人对事情比较熟悉。

examples.zh: 这件事交给老王办吧，他老马识途。
examples.en: Give this to Old Wang — he knows the ropes.

examples.zh: 老马识途，听听前辈的意见。
examples.en: Experience counts — listen to the old hands.

story.en: Returning from a campaign, Duke Huan of Qi's army got lost. Guan Zhong said: "An old horse's wisdom can be used" — they let old horses lead and found the road.
story.zh: 齐桓公征伐归途中迷路，管仲说："老马之智可用也。"于是放开老马，跟着它找到了路。

natural: Courteous to the worthy, humble to scholars

meaning.en: (Of a leader) to treat talented people with respect.
meaning.zh: 对有才德的人以礼相待，对一般有才能的人不计自己的身份去结交。

examples.zh: 这位老板礼贤下士，吸引了很多人才。
examples.en: The boss values talent and has attracted many able people.

examples.zh: 刘备礼贤下士，三顾茅庐请诸葛亮。
examples.en: Liu Bei respected talent and visited Zhuge Liang three times.

natural: Jade nectar and jade liquid

meaning.en: Fine wine; nectar.
meaning.zh: 用美玉制成的浆液。比喻美酒或甘美的浆汁。

examples.zh: 这壶酒简直是琼浆玉液。
examples.en: This wine is nectar of the gods.

examples.zh: 在沙漠里，一口清水胜过琼浆玉液。
examples.en: In the desert, a sip of clean water beats the finest wine.

natural: Striking straight at Huanglong

meaning.en: To strike at the heart of the enemy.
meaning.zh: 直接攻到敌人的老巢。

equivalents: take the fight to the enemy

examples.zh: 我军乘胜追击，直捣黄龙。
examples.en: Our army pressed on and struck at the enemy's heart.

examples.zh: 这家公司直捣黄龙，打进了对手的大本营市场。
examples.en: The company went for the jugular, entering its rival's home market.

story.en: General Yue Fei promised his troops: "Let us strike straight to Huanglong Prefecture and drink our fill together!" — Huanglong being the Jurchen Jin heartland.
story.zh: 岳飞对部下说："直抵黄龙府，与诸君痛饮尔！"黄龙府是金国腹地。

natural: Expression unchanged

meaning.en: Calm and composed; unflustered.
meaning.zh: 神情脸色跟平常一样。形容遇事镇静。

examples.zh: 面对质问，他神色自若。
examples.en: Faced with the questioning, he was unflustered.

examples.zh: 虽然心里紧张，她表面上神色自若。
examples.en: Though nervous inside, she appeared perfectly calm.

natural: Carrying firewood to fight a fire

meaning.en: To make things worse by the wrong remedy.
meaning.zh: 抱着柴草去救火。比喻用错误的方法去消除灾祸，结果使灾祸扩大。

equivalents: a cure worse than the disease

examples.zh: 用借钱来还债，无异于抱薪救火。
examples.en: Borrowing to pay debts only adds fuel to the fire.

examples.zh: 这种政策是抱薪救火，问题会更严重。
examples.en: This policy will make matters worse.

story.en: Su Dai warned the King of Wei against ceding land to Qin to buy peace: "Serving Qin with land is like carrying firewood to put out a fire — the fire won't go out till the wood is gone."
story.zh: 苏代对魏王说："以地事秦，譬犹抱薪救火，薪不尽，火不灭。"

natural: Dull-headed and dull-brained

meaning.en: Dim-witted; slow on the uptake.
meaning.zh: 形容思想、行动迟钝笨拙。

examples.zh: 他看起来呆头呆脑的，其实很聪明。
examples.en: He looks a bit dopey but is actually very clever.

examples.zh: 别呆头呆脑地站着，快来帮忙！
examples.en: Don't just stand there gawping — come and help!

usage.en: Predicate or adverbial. Colloquial; can be affectionate.

natural: Every morning and every evening

meaning.en: Day and night; constantly (especially of lovers together).
meaning.zh: 每天早晨和晚上。指天天如此，也指恋人朝夕相处。

examples.zh: 两情若是久长时，又岂在朝朝暮暮。
examples.en: If love between two is to last forever, why need they be together day and night?

examples.zh: 他们朝朝暮暮生活在一起。
examples.en: They live together day in, day out.

origin.source: 战国·宋玉《高唐赋》；宋·秦观《鹊桥仙》

story.en: Song Yu's goddess said she would be "morning clouds and evening rain, morning after morning, evening after evening". Qin Guan's Qixi lyric made it famous: true love needn't mean being together every morning and evening.
story.zh: 宋玉《高唐赋》："旦为朝云，暮为行雨，朝朝暮暮，阳台之下。"秦观《鹊桥仙》："两情若是久长时，又岂在朝朝暮暮。"

usage.en: Adverbial or object. 朝 is zhāo.
usage.zh: 多作状语、宾语。"朝"读 zhāo。

natural: Tying one's hair to the beam and jabbing one's thigh

meaning.en: To study with extreme diligence.
meaning.zh: 形容刻苦学习。

examples.zh: 古人悬梁刺股，刻苦读书。
examples.en: Ancient scholars went to extreme lengths to stay awake and study.

examples.zh: 备考不必悬梁刺股，但要坚持。
examples.en: You needn't torture yourself revising, but you must keep at it.

story.en: Sun Jing tied his hair to a roof beam so he'd be jerked awake if he nodded off while reading; Su Qin jabbed his thigh with an awl when he got sleepy.
story.zh: 孙敬读书时用绳子把头发系在房梁上，防止打瞌睡；苏秦读书困了就用锥子刺大腿。
